sentences.en: a pigeon roost in your house or, you know, nearby.
sentences.zh: 在家里或附近有个鸽棚。

sentences.en: And so they spread with the upper cruSt.
sentences.zh: 所以它们随着上层社会传播开来。

sentences.en: But then they became really successful.
sentences.zh: 但后来它们变得非常成功。

sentences.en: And as America became more and more successful
sentences.zh: 随着美国越来越繁荣，

sentences.en: and we started producing more and more food
sentences.zh: 我们开始生产越来越多的食物，

sentences.en: and started building these plazas
sentences.zh: 开始建造这些广场，

sentences.en: with statues in the middle of them,
sentences.zh: 中间还立着雕像，

sentences.en: pigeons started taking to those places
sentences.zh: 鸽子开始占据这些地方，

sentences.en: and taking them over.
sentences.zh: 并接管了它们。

sentences.en: And you can't really maintain your status
sentences.zh: 你不可能维持你的地位，

sentences.en: as a symbol of the aristocracy
sentences.zh: 作为贵族的象征，

sentences.en: if you're an incredibly common thing.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一种极其普通的东西的话。

sentences.en: And so they fell from grace.
sentences.zh: 于是它们失宠了。

sentences.en: And you can see this happening in the language too.
sentences.zh: 你也能在语言中看到这种变化。

sentences.en: One of the interesting things about pigeons
sentences.zh: 关于鸽子，有趣的一点是，

sentences.en: is the words pigeon and dove,
sentences.zh: “pigeon”和“dove”这两个词，

sentences.en: for a long time they were just mixed together.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里它们是混用的。

sentences.en: There's no scientific distinction
sentences.zh: 在科学上并没有什么区别，

sentences.en: between those two things.
sentences.zh: 界定这两者。

sentences.en: You know, it's all kind of the same family.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它们其实属于同一个科。

sentences.en: Often the common name of something
sentences.zh: 通常某种东西的俗名，

sentences.en: will both be a pigeon and a dove.
sentences.zh: 既可以叫pigeon也可以叫dove。

sentences.en: But at some point, everything good was a dove
sentences.zh: 但在某个时刻，所有美好的东西都成了dove，

sentences.en: and everything bad was a pigeon.
sentences.zh: 而所有糟糕的东西都成了pigeon。

sentences.en: And you can see it today.
sentences.zh: 今天你依然能看到这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, if you try and change it around,
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果你试着互换一下，

sentences.en: there's this huge cultural antipathy toward pigeons, right?
sentences.zh: 人们对鸽子有一种巨大的文化反感，对吧？

sentences.en: So if you think of, like, pigeon soap
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想到，比如，鸽子香皂，

sentences.en: or pigeon chocolate bars,
sentences.zh: 或者鸽子巧克力棒，

sentences.en: it just doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 这根本行不通。

sentences.en: Or you could think about it in, like,
sentences.zh: 或者你可以想想，比如，

sentences.en: the uses in the Bible,
sentences.zh: 它们在《圣经》中的用法，

sentences.en: like the Holy Spirit descending from heaven
sentences.zh: 比如圣灵从天而降，

sentences.en: in the form of a pigeon.
sentences.zh: 以鸽子的形式出现。

sentences.en: And so they've undergone this radical transformation.
sentences.zh: 所以它们经历了一场彻底的转变。

sentences.en: And I sort of feel for them.
sentences.zh: 我多少有点同情它们。

sentences.en: If you look at them closely,
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细观察它们，

sentences.en: they're these beautiful birds,
sentences.zh: 它们是美丽的鸟儿，

sentences.en: if they're not diseased and rabid.
sentences.zh: 如果它们没有染病或狂躁的话。

sentences.en: We're kind of in this cold war,
sentences.zh: 我们一直处于这种冷战中，

sentences.en: maybe even a hot war with pigeons all the time.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能是一场与鸽子的热战。

sentences.en: And it doesn't really work all that well.
sentences.zh: 而且效果并不怎么好。

sentences.en: So what are the ways that we deal with pigeons?
sentences.zh: 那么我们处理鸽子的方法有哪些呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So the pigeon control industry
sentences.zh: 鸽子防治行业

sentences.en: is a pretty massive industry.
sentences.zh: 是一个相当庞大的产业。

sentences.en: And you can do a lot of things.
sentences.zh: 你可以做很多事情。

sentences.en: You can put spikes out to stop the pigeons.
sentences.zh: 你可以安装尖刺来阻止鸽子。

sentences.en: You can put netting that blocks them.
sentences.zh: 你可以安装网来阻挡它们。

sentences.en: They even have, like, miniature electric fences
sentences.zh: 它们甚至还有微型电网，

sentences.en: to keep pigeons away.
sentences.zh: 用来驱赶鸽子。

sentences.en: And none of it works.
sentences.zh: 但都没用。

sentences.en: I mean, it all works to a certain degree
sentences.zh: 我是说，它们在一定程度上是有效的，

sentences.en: in that you can push pigeons off of one building,
sentences.zh: 你可以把鸽子从一栋楼赶走，

sentences.en: but they can just go to the next building.
sentences.zh: 但它们只会飞到下一栋楼。

sentences.en: And that's what they do.
sentences.zh: 它们就是这么做的。

sentences.en: And as long as the food source is there,
sentences.zh: 只要食物来源还在，

sentences.en: the pigeons will be there.
sentences.zh: 鸽子就会在那里。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay, so let's get on to the pigeon milk.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们来谈谈鸽乳吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Please.
sentences.zh: 请讲。

sentences.en: I read this,
sentences.zh: 我读到这个的时候，

sentences.en: and it was really upsetting to me.
sentences.zh: 真的让我感到很不舒服。

sentences.en: So I want you to upset all these people here in this room.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望你也能让在座的各位感到不舒服。

sentences.en: What is pigeon milk?
sentences.zh: 什么是鸽乳？

sentences.en: So normally we think of mammals giving milk.
sentences.zh: 通常我们认为哺乳动物才会分泌乳汁。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: But it's a really useful delivery device of nutrients,
sentences.zh: 但这是一种非常有效的营养输送方式，

sentences.en: and birds have figured it out, too,
sentences.zh: 鸟类也发现了这一点，

sentences.en: or at least pigeons have figured it out, too.
sentences.zh: 或者至少鸽子发现了这一点。

sentences.en: And it's completely convergent evolution.
sentences.zh: 这完全是趋同进化。

sentences.en: It's not like this is something
sentences.zh: 这并不是说这是某种

sentences.en: that has spread up the evolutionary tree.
sentences.zh: 沿着进化树传播下来的东西。

sentences.en: It's very similar in its structure,
sentences.zh: 它的结构非常相似，

sentences.en: but it's completely independently derived.
sentences.zh: 但却是完全独立演化出来的。

sentences.en: And essentially what happens is
sentences.zh: 本质上发生的情况是，

sentences.en: the birds secrete some nutrients
sentences.zh: 鸟类通过喉咙内部

sentences.en: through the inside of their throats,
sentences.zh: 分泌一些营养物质，

sentences.en: and there's a little pouch that birds have
sentences.zh: 鸟类喉咙里有一个小囊，

sentences.en: inside their throats called the crop,
sentences.zh: 叫做嗉囊，

sentences.en: and it collects in the crop,
sentences.zh: 它会聚集在嗉囊里，

sentences.en: and it's this sort of yellowish, cheesy...
sentences.zh: 这是一种黄色的、奶酪状的……

sentences.en: Yeah, not gross at all.
sentences.zh: 是啊，一点都不恶心。

sentences.en: You're right.
sentences.zh: 你说得对。

sentences.en: And then the squabs, the little birds,
sentences.zh: 然后幼鸽，也就是小鸟，

sentences.en: stick their heads down the parents' throats
sentences.zh: 把头伸进父母的喉咙里，

sentences.en: and thrust to get the pigeon milk out.
sentences.zh: 用力挤压以获取鸽乳。

sentences.en: Both the males and the females produce this.
sentences.zh: 雄鸽和雌鸽都会分泌这种物质。

sentences.en: It's a beautiful wonder of nature.
sentences.zh: 这是大自然美丽的奇迹。

sentences.en: When you were researching pigeons,
sentences.zh: 当你研究鸽子的时候，

sentences.en: you noticed that a bunch of them have messed up legs.
sentences.zh: 你注意到很多鸽子的腿都畸形了。

sentences.en: And there's a mystery to why
sentences.zh: 为什么会有这么多鸽子

sentences.en: so many pigeons have messed up legs.
sentences.zh: 腿部畸形，这还是个谜。

sentences.en: Yeah, so I don't know if you've seen this,
sentences.zh: 是啊，我不知道你有没有见过，

sentences.en: but I started seeing this
sentences.zh: 但我开始注意到这一点了。

sentences.en: as soon as I started looking closely at pigeons,
sentences.zh: 当我开始仔细观察鸽子时，

sentences.en: that they often would be missing a toe,
sentences.zh: 我发现它们经常缺一根脚趾，

sentences.en: or they'd be missing their foot entirely,
sentences.zh: 或者整个脚掌都没了，

sentences.en: and it was just this stump.
sentences.zh: 只剩下一个残肢。

sentences.en: And it was like this huge percentage.
sentences.zh: 而且比例高得惊人。

sentences.en: Every time I would look,
sentences.zh: 每次我观察时，

sentences.en: I would see there'd be like 10 pigeons out there,
sentences.zh: 我都会看到大概有10只鸽子在那里，

sentences.en: and one or two of them
sentences.zh: 其中一两只

sentences.en: would have something wrong with their feet.
sentences.zh: 脚部会有问题。

sentences.en: And when I started looking for the answers about this,
sentences.zh: 当我开始寻找原因时，

sentences.en: I found all of these ideas,
sentences.zh: 我找到了各种各样的说法，

sentences.en: and people were pretty sure that there were predators,
sentences.zh: 人们很确定是有捕食者，

sentences.en: like cats were attacking their feet.
sentences.zh: 比如猫会攻击它们的脚。

sentences.en: But why would they just attack the feet?
sentences.zh: 但为什么偏偏只攻击脚呢？

sentences.en: Or they were getting staph infections.
sentences.zh: 还有人说是得了葡萄球菌感染。

sentences.en: And it took me a really long time to figure this out.
sentences.zh: 我花了很长时间才弄明白这件事。

sentences.en: It was sort of throughout the entire course of the research
sentences.zh: 这几乎贯穿了整个研究过程，

sentences.en: I was tracing down these different threads.
sentences.zh: 我一直在追踪这些不同的线索。

sentences.en: And eventually what I found,
sentences.zh: 最终我发现，

sentences.en: the premier pigeon researcher said,
sentences.zh: 那位顶尖的鸽子研究员说，

sentences.en: oh yes, all of this is nonsense.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，这些全是无稽之谈。

sentences.en: What happens is that they pick up little bits of thread,
sentences.zh: 真相是它们会捡起一些细线，

sentences.en: or hair, which is incredibly common in cities,
sentences.zh: 或是头发，这在城市里非常普遍，

sentences.en: and it gets tangled around their feet,
sentences.zh: 线缠绕在它们的脚上，

sentences.en: and they don't have any way to get it off.
sentences.zh: 而它们没有任何办法弄掉。

sentences.en: And it just gets tangled tighter and tighter,
sentences.zh: 线会越缠越紧，

sentences.en: and it causes these lesions.
sentences.zh: 从而导致这些病变。

sentences.en: And normally birds don't get this
sentences.zh: 通常鸟类不会这样，

sentences.en: because most birds hop and pigeons kind of shuffle.
sentences.zh: 因为大多数鸟是跳着走的，而鸽子是挪着走的。

sentences.en: And so they're really well adapted to cities in many ways,
sentences.zh: 所以它们在很多方面非常适应城市生活，

sentences.en: except for this one terrible, grotesque flaw.
sentences.zh: 除了这一个可怕且怪异的缺陷。

sentences.en: For some reason, their beak's just,
sentences.zh: 出于某种原因，它们的喙就是，

sentences.en: they're not capable of taking them.
sentences.zh: 它们无法处理这些东西。

sentences.en: They're not capable of untangling it.
sentences.zh: 它们无法解开缠绕。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Oh, that's sad.
sentences.zh: 哦，真可怜。

sentences.en: Okay, I feel bad for pigeons now.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我现在开始同情鸽子了。

sentences.en: In the book, most of the flora and fauna
sentences.zh: 在书中，大部分动植物

sentences.en: are species that thrive in the concrete landscape,
sentences.zh: 都是在混凝土景观中茁壮成长的物种，

sentences.en: but humans didn't purposely make it easy for them to survive.
sentences.zh: 但人类并不是刻意让它们容易生存的。

sentences.en: That's not the case for the ginkgo biloba,
sentences.zh: 银杏树的情况则不同，

sentences.en: which is a tree that probably wouldn't exist anymore
sentences.zh: 如果不是因为人们在城市里种植它们，

sentences.en: if it weren't for people planting them in cities.
sentences.zh: 这种树可能早就灭绝了。

sentences.en: So why are ginkgos unsuitable for nature,
sentences.zh: 那么为什么银杏不适合自然环境，

sentences.en: and why do they do so well in cities?
sentences.zh: 却在城市里长得这么好呢？

sentences.en: The golden age of ginkgos was the Cretaceous,
sentences.zh: 银杏的黄金时代是白垩纪，

sentences.en: when ginkgos ruled the world, as we all know.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，那时银杏统治着世界。

sentences.en: That's how we think of that era.
sentences.zh: 我们对那个时代的印象就是这样。

sentences.en: They just shared it with dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 它们只是和恐龙共享那个时代。

sentences.en: They didn't care.
sentences.zh: 它们根本不在乎。

sentences.en: Really, they were in charge.
sentences.zh: 说真的，它们才是主宰。

sentences.en: At that time, ginkgos had some evolutionary partner.
sentences.zh: 那时，银杏有一些进化伙伴。

sentences.en: They had some kind of creature
sentences.zh: 它们有某种生物

sentences.en: that would help them distribute their seeds.
sentences.zh: 会帮助它们传播种子。

sentences.en: And today, we have no idea what this is.
sentences.zh: 而今天，我们完全不知道那是什么。

sentences.en: It's this mystery that people are still trying to figure out.
sentences.zh: 这是一个人们仍在试图解开的谜团。

sentences.en: And it's a double mystery,
sentences.zh: 而且这是一个双重谜团，

sentences.en: because their seeds smell like a microwave to death.
sentences.zh: 因为它们的种子闻起来简直臭不可闻。

sentences.en: It's just terrible.
sentences.zh: 简直太糟糕了。

sentences.en: There's male and female ginkgos,
sentences.zh: 银杏有雌雄之分，

sentences.en: and the females produce the seeds.
sentences.zh: 雌树会结出种子。

sentences.en: And if you're around them around September, November,
sentences.zh: 如果你在九月到十一月期间待在它们附近，

sentences.en: you'll notice.
sentences.zh: 你就会注意到。

sentences.en: That's one thing you can open your eyes to.
sentences.zh: 这是你可以留意的一件事。

sentences.en: You can stop and find the seeds
sentences.zh: 你可以停下来找找种子，

sentences.en: and notice just how terrible they smell.
sentences.zh: 感受一下它们闻起来有多糟糕。

sentences.en: But there was something that must have liked this smell
sentences.zh: 但肯定有什么东西喜欢这种气味，

sentences.en: and must have eaten it and carried it to different places.
sentences.zh: 并且吃掉它，把它带到不同的地方。

sentences.en: And at some point, the seed distributor probably died out.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，这种种子传播者可能灭绝了。

sentences.en: And it simply meant that the ginkgos couldn't outrun the glaciers
sentences.zh: 这意味着银杏无法在气候变化时

sentences.en: as the climate changed.
sentences.zh: 逃过冰川的侵袭。

sentences.en: And so you see them all across the world.
sentences.zh: 所以你会在世界各地看到它们。

sentences.en: They have these really tough, leathery leaves,
sentences.zh: 它们有非常坚韧、皮革般的叶子，

sentences.en: so they make great fossils.
sentences.zh: 所以它们能形成很好的化石。

sentences.en: And people find them all over the place.
sentences.zh: 人们到处都能发现它们。

sentences.en: And then they retreat and they retreat and they retreat
sentences.zh: 然后它们不断退缩，不断退缩，

sentences.en: until they're just a couple valleys in China where they're left.
sentences.zh: 直到只剩下中国境内的几个山谷。

sentences.en: And their entire family gets wiped out, too.
sentences.zh: 它们的整个家族也随之灭绝了。

sentences.en: They're the only remaining species
sentences.zh: 它们是整个植物门类中

sentences.en: of this whole division of plant life that remains.
sentences.zh: 仅存的唯一物种。

sentences.en: And then people come along,
sentences.zh: 然后人类出现了，

sentences.en: and people fall in love with ginkgos.
sentences.zh: 人们爱上了银杏。

sentences.en: And it turns out that ginkgos kind of love us, too.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，银杏也挺喜欢我们的。

sentences.en: They can thrive in polluted air.
sentences.zh: 它们能在污染的空气中茁壮成长。

sentences.en: They do well in concrete.
sentences.zh: 它们在混凝土环境中长得很好。

sentences.en: They do well in partial light,
sentences.zh: 它们在部分光照下也能生长，

sentences.en: which is perfect for cities.
sentences.zh: 这对城市来说非常完美。

sentences.en: They're famously good at taking abuse,
sentences.zh: 它们以耐折腾而闻名，

sentences.en: being backed into by a delivery truck
sentences.zh: 无论是被送货卡车撞到，

sentences.en: or close to an atom bomb.
sentences.zh: 还是靠近原子弹爆炸点。

sentences.en: There's one just a kilometer away
sentences.zh: 距离广岛原子弹爆炸中心仅一公里处，

sentences.en: from the Hiroshima bomb site that survived and regrew.
sentences.zh: 就有一棵银杏幸存并重新生长。

sentences.en: It's this kind of amazing story
sentences.zh: 这是一个令人惊叹的故事，

sentences.en: where they just barely hung on for millions and millions of years.
sentences.zh: 它们在数百万年的时间里勉强存活了下来。

sentences.en: And then they happen to find themselves
sentences.zh: 然后它们恰好发现自己

sentences.en: in this crazy point in the Earth's history
sentences.zh: 处于地球历史上这个疯狂的节点，

sentences.en: where they could thrive in human cities.
sentences.zh: 在这里它们可以在人类城市中茁壮成长。

sentences.en: Because the fruits, the seeds are so stinky,
sentences.zh: 因为果实和种子太臭了，

sentences.en: we tend to plant only the male species, right?
sentences.zh: 我们倾向于只种植雄性品种，对吧？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: People try to just plant the males,
sentences.zh: 人们试图只种雄树，

sentences.en: and sometimes they get it wrong.
sentences.zh: 但有时会弄错。

sentences.en: And it's hard.
sentences.zh: 这很难。

sentences.en: It's like 30 years before they become sexually mature,
sentences.zh: 它们要长30年才达到性成熟，

sentences.en: so then it's like, oops.
sentences.zh: 所以到时候就会发现，哎呀，

sentences.en: I guess that was a female.
sentences.zh: 原来那是棵雌树。

sentences.en: But even the males have their downsides
sentences.zh: 但即使是雄树也有缺点，

sentences.en: because then they produce tons and tons of pollen.
sentences.zh: 因为它们会产生大量的花粉。

sentences.en: So one way or the other.
sentences.zh: 所以怎么着都不行。

sentences.en: So you discovered that ginkgo seeds were edible at a certain point
sentences.zh: 所以你发现银杏种子在某种程度上是可以食用的，

sentences.en: once you get rid of that really stinky flesh that's around them.
sentences.zh: 只要去掉周围那层非常臭的果肉。

sentences.en: And I just have this quote that I want to read from your book,
sentences.zh: 我刚好想读一段你书里的引文，

sentences.en: which I really liked a lot.
sentences.zh: 我非常喜欢这一段。

sentences.en: It says,
